ishango.alt: Ishango bone, an Upper Paleolithic bone tool with rows of notches, possibly an early counting device.

plimpton.alt: Plimpton 322, a Babylonian clay tablet listing Pythagorean triples in cuneiform columns.

euclid.alt: Oxyrhynchus papyrus fragment of Euclid's Elements written in Greek on papyrus.

haytham.alt: Engraved title page of the Latin Opticae Thesaurus, Ibn al-Haytham's optics, showing ships set alight.

copernicus.alt: Diagram of the heliocentric solar system from Copernicus's De revolutionibus, with the Sun at centre.
copernicus.credit: Nicolaus Copernicus, De revolutionibus (1543), scan via Wikimedia Commons

galileo.alt: Galileo's ink-wash sketches of the Moon's surface, drawn through his telescope in 1609.

hooke.alt: Hooke's Micrographia engraving of cork cells seen through a microscope, with a mimosa leaf below.

fraunhofer.alt: Solar spectrum with labelled dark Fraunhofer absorption lines from A to K.

darwin.alt: Charles Darwin's 1837 notebook sketch of a branching tree with the words 'I think'.

rontgen.alt: Early X-ray photograph of a hand with rings, taken by Wilhelm Röntgen in December 1895.

relativity.alt: Solar eclipse photograph from the 1919 expedition that tested general relativity.
relativity.credit: Frank Watson Dyson / Arthur Eddington / Charles Rundle Davidson

quantum.alt: Group photograph of the 1927 Solvay Conference on electrons and photons, with leading physicists.

transistor.alt: Replica of the first point-contact transistor, built at Bell Labs in 1947.
transistor.credit: US government photograph, via Wikimedia Commons

apollo.alt: Buzz Aldrin standing on the lunar surface during Apollo 11, photographed by Neil Armstrong.

voyager.alt: The Pale Blue Dot, Earth as a tiny speck seen by Voyager 1 from about six billion kilometres.

jwst.alt: Webb's First Deep Field of the SMACS 0723 galaxy cluster, with lensed background galaxies.

ligo.alt: Strain signals from the twin LIGO detectors for the first detected gravitational wave, GW150914.

higgs.alt: Simulated CMS detector event display of a candidate Higgs boson decay.
